html:
Studenica is a Serbian Orthodox monastery in central Serbia, southwest of Kraljevo, founded around 1190 by the Serbian ruler Stefan Nemanja. It is the mother church of medieval Serbian art.

Nemanja united the Serbian lands and founded the Nemanjić dynasty, which ruled for two hundred years. In 1196 he gave up his throne to his son and became a monk, first at Studenica and then on Mount Athos, where he and his son Sava founded the Serbian monastery of Hilandar. He was buried at Studenica and honoured as a saint, and the monastery became the spiritual centre of the state.

Its Church of the Virgin mixes styles: white marble outside in the Romanesque manner of the Adriatic coast, with a Byzantine plan and dome. Inside, frescoes painted in 1208 and 1209 include a famous Crucifixion. Sava wrote the monastery's rule and a life of his father there. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
sum: Studenica is a Serbian Orthodox monastery in central Serbia, southwest of Kraljevo, founded around 1190 by the Serbian ruler Stefan Nemanja. It is the mother church of medieval Serbian art.
